open_issues: Finding 4 / missing spec item «متابعات … تذكير» is NOT fixed and cannot be from this package: the fix is a correspondence follow-up pass inside src/Wakeel.Core/Services/ReminderScheduler.cs, which is outside this package's allowed paths and is currently modified by another agent. Everything it needs is public: IFollowUpService.RunDueRemindersAsync(now) is idempotent and tested, or the scheduler can raise the notifications itself with ReminderScheduler.Key(FollowUpService.ReminderKeyKind, followup.Id, followup.ReminderAt.Value), FollowUpService.ReminderKind, CoreAr.CorrFollowupReminderTitle, CoreAr.CorrFollowupReminderBody(subject), CorrespondenceService.AuditEntityType. Until that call lands, a stored follow-up reminder never rings. Needs assignment to the owner of ReminderScheduler.cs, or an explicit grant of that file to the B3 builder.

Finding 12 is a docs decision, not code: DATA-MODEL §0 line 23 still names correspondence.official_number as an unfiltered unique index, while migration 0003 replaced it with UNIQUE(direction, official_number) (ARCHITECTURE §5's two independent sequences make the same number text legitimate for one incoming and one outgoing letter on the same day). docs/ is outside this package's write scope — the schema/docs owner should amend §0 to «(direction, official_number)».

«حذف المسودة غير المرقّمة نهائيًا» (AGREEMENT item 19) remains a soft delete, as reported in the previous round: DATA-MODEL §0 forbids physically deleting a synced row and correspondence has only AFTER INSERT/UPDATE change_log triggers, so a physical DELETE would never reach the other devices and the draft would return on the next sync. The user experience is identical (global query filter, no restore command). Still needs the owner's ratification or a schema change (AFTER DELETE trigger + sync rule).
notes:
Every high/medium/low finding inside this package's paths is fixed, each with a test.

Finding 1 (high) — CorrectionService.ApplyAsync no longer mutates the tracked row while still deciding. The loop is split into a validation pass that whitelists the field, reads the old value, skips no-ops and PARSES the new value into a PlannedChange carrying an Action<CorrespondenceRow> that can only assign; every refusal (uncorrectable field, unreadable date, unknown confidentiality, cleared subject) is raised there, before the first write. A second pass then applies every planned change. Test A_batch_that_fails_part_way_writes_nothing_even_after_a_later_save sends subject+bad date together, expects the refusal, then runs an unrelated FollowUps.AddAsync save and asserts the subject is unchanged and Corrections is empty.

Finding 2 (medium) — DuplicateCandidate gained PartyNameSnapshot (filled from row.PartyNameSnapshot in CorrespondenceService.Candidate) and SameParty gained a third arm: with no PartyId and no UnitId on the candidate, ArabicText.Normalize of both party-name snapshots decides, id comparisons still first. Three tests: the same typed-name letter registered twice is refused with CoreAr.CorrDuplicateExact (not the wrong «الرقم نفسه مسجَّل لجهة أخرى») and the incoming sequence stays at 1; a ة/tatweel spelling variant is still the same party; a genuinely different typed body with the same number is still only a suspected review.

Finding 3 (medium) — ExchangeService.ImportAsync wraps RegisterIncomingAsync in try/catch and calls correspondence.DeleteDraftAsync (via a DiscardDraftAsync helper using CancellationToken.None and swallowing its own failure) before rethrowing, so a refused registration leaves no stray unnumbered draft. One transaction around both was impossible — RegisterIncomingAsync opens its own and EF/SQLite does not nest. Test An_import_that_is_refused_leaves_no_draft_behind hand-registers a colliding incoming (tatweel spelling, so the exact «already imported» pre-check does not fire but the normalised duplicate check does), expects CorrDuplicateExact, and asserts the only stored row is the hand-registered one and the sequence is still 1.

Finding 5 (medium) — CorrectionEntry is now purely the stored JSON shape; CorrectionView.Changes is a list of the new CorrectionFieldView(Field, FieldLabelAr, Old, OldAr, New, NewAr). OldAr/NewAr run confidentiality through CorrespondenceAr.Confidentiality and dates through ArabicRelativeTime.DateTimeText; the raw Old/New strings and the stored corrections.changes payload are unchanged. Test The_correction_record_is_read_in_arabic_not_in_enum_names_or_iso_dates covers both the fresh result and the reloaded one.

Finding 6 (medium) — CoreAr.CorrCorrectionFieldUnknown now takes an Arabic label, fed by the new CorrespondenceAr.FieldLabel map over the new CoreAr.CorrField* labels; an unrecognised key gets CorrCorrectionFieldNotCorrectable, so no English identifier reaches the user. ParseDate/ParseConfidentiality now use the new CorrCorrectionBadDate and CorrCorrectionBadConfidentiality. Three tests, including the updated A_field_that_may_not_be_corrected_is_refused_and_nothing_is_written which also asserts the message does not contain "officialNumber".

Finding 7 (low) — CancelAsync on an unnumbered draft throws the new CoreAr.CorrRefusedCancelDraft («المسودة غير المرقّمة تُحذف ولا تُلغى»); the test also proves the delete command does apply.

Finding 8 (low) — SetRecipientOnlyAsync and SetLinksAsync now write audit rows (new actions correspondence.recipient_only and correspondence.links_changed, new CoreAr summaries), and only when the value actually changed, so a form re-posting the same value writes nothing. Two tests assert the row counts and summaries.

Finding 9 (low) — ExportAsync refuses a cancelled letter with the new CoreAr.CorrExchangeCancelled; test approves, cancels, expects the refusal and asserts no outgoing exchange-log row.

Finding 10 (low) — the import preview now says CoreAr.CorrExchangeSignatureExternal for a package from another organisation and keeps «التوقيع سليم» only where the chain was actually checked against the pinned organisation key; the SignatureAr XML doc was updated and a test pins both.

Finding 11 (low) — FollowUpService.RunDueRemindersAsync now narrows the open-correspondence read to the ids actually due and replaces the per-entry AnyAsync with a single StartsWith(ReminderScheduler.KeyPrefix) read over a bounded window kept in a HashSet. The existing idempotence tests pass unchanged.
